lines: It's Monday morning in Singapore.
Maya runs a sales team of six, with hundreds of leads, and no time.
Leads go cold in the CRM. Research eats the whole morning.
And nobody is sure which companies are even real.
Meet Sales Mama.
An AI sales harness that runs inside Claude Code. The repo is the system.
At two a.m., scouts scan news, tenders and registries.
Every lead is scored, and a virtual account manager watches each book.
At eight thirty, the manager opens the cockpit.
Last night's run, the hot accounts, and a fair allocation, approved in one click.
Reps type, mama day.
Replies are triaged, new accounts are researched in parallel, and drafts are written in their own voice.
Every fact links back to its source. No source, no claim.
In the send window, mama send shows the whole batch.
The rep picks, approves once, and Sales Mama sends email and WhatsApp, logging every touch.
Nothing goes out without approval.
Before anyone sells, company check asks: is this company real?
Live with ACRA, filing on time, a real office, not a virtual one, and more than three staff.
Three verifier agents gather the evidence.
Ask a question, get a report.
Nine thousand six hundred clinics. Ninety-three percent filing on time. And the best new leads.
Guardrails are built in: approvals, citations, suppression lists, and rules for every market.
Sales Mama.
Your sales team's morning, done before coffee.
